text:
incident-bot: PAGING emily (oncall) - alert: elevated KV cache prefix lookup latencies (>1.2s p95) and increased 5xx for prefix reads across us-west-2. svc: inference-prefix-cache, impact: some tenants seeing generation failures and long tails. runbook link: https://confluence.redwood/ops/prefix-cache-issues

alex: I see the same in dashboards. hotkey traffic to a handful of tenants spiking. looks like a small set of prefixes causing high miss+storage churn.

emily: picking up. are we seeing backend throttles or upstream storage errors?

sanjay: storage backend (tier2-kv) is fine, but cache eviction pressure skyrocketed — continuous misses causing heavy backend fanout. not immediate storage OOM but lots of cross-AZ latency.

cora: confirmed errors for tenant:turbine-prod and tenant:studio-eu. errors are timeouts from KV read path, leading to 502 on/near prefix lookup. customers flagged via monitoring.

emily: status: declare incident. tagging SRE. immediate mitigation ideas: 1) quarantine hot prefixes (bypass cache for those prefixes -> serve from safe fallback), 2) apply per-tenant rate limiting to reduce fanout, 3) temporarily disable prefix prefetching/autopopulate, 4) manual eviction of very large keys.

alex: +1 quarantine hot prefixes. if we bypass cache for hot prefixes, we avoid thrashing the cache and protect others. however bypass increases backend load for those tenants — need limits.

ops-bot: runbook action queued: create incident channel #incident-1801234567; set priority P1; notify ENG-SRE and PL.

emily: plan: step 1) identify top 10 prefixes by miss rate and traffic. step 2) enable quarantine mode for those prefixes (cache bypass + soft rate cap 50r/s). step 3) create a traffic-shape to route their requests to fallback pool with smaller concurrency. step 4) monitor errors and tail latencies for global. assign tasks.

jamie: I can run the prefix list query: ```
# query top prefixes by miss rate
SELECT prefix, miss_rate, rps FROM metrics.prefix_cache WHERE window=5m ORDER BY miss_rate DESC LIMIT 20;
```

alex: after we have the list, we use the ops command to quarantine: ```
# quarantine command
opsctl cache quarantine-set --prefix "tenant:XXXX:*" --mode bypass --rate-limit 50 --reason "hotkey mitigation"
```

emily: sanjay, can you prepare the fallback pool config? make sure fallback_pool has reduced concurrency (max_concurrency=4) and circuit-breaker at 5xx>3%

sanjay: will do. prepping a small pool in us-west-2. also recommend temporarily increase tenant request quotas for affected customers so we can throttle instead of dropping.

cora: customer comms: two customers already alerted via health webhook. recommend we open support tickets and provide ETA ~30m. I can draft message.

jamie: got top prefixes: tenant:turbine-prod:cmd (rps 180, miss_rate 0.78), tenant:studio-eu:ctx (rps 120, miss_rate 0.71), tenant:atlas:bot-session (rps 95, miss_rate 0.66), plus a tail of ~7 others.

emily: executing quarantine for top 10 now. running opsctl commands one-by-one and monitoring.

alex: note: we should also flip on temporary optimistic-prefetch=false for everyone to stop autopopulate. config name: prefix_cache.opt_prefetch -> false.

ops-bot: command executed: opsctl cache quarantine-set --prefix "tenant:turbine-prod:*" --mode bypass --rate-limit 50 --issued_by emily --correlation 1801234567

emily: quarantine applied to turbine-prod, studio-eu, atlas and 7 others. routing updated: those prefixes will bypass cache and hit fallback pool with rate limit 50r/s.

cora: customer comms sent to affected tenants (turbine-prod, studio-eu, atlas) via support, flagged as P1 incident.

jamie: monitoring: global p95 for prefix lookup dropped from 1.2s -> 480ms in last 2 minutes. 5xx count decreased by ~60% for non-affected tenants. affected tenants still see higher backend latency but fewer 502s.

emily: good. next: apply soft per-tenant throttle for those prefix groups to smooth backend load. using rate-limit policy: tenant_throttle.v1 -> 30r/s burst 10.

alex: also schedule manual eviction of a large key we found: `tenant:turbine-prod:ctx:huge-blob` size 980MB - evicting to reduce storage churn. command: ```
opsctl cache evict-key --key "tenant:turbine-prod:ctx:huge-blob" --force --issued_by emily
```

ops-bot: eviction queued. warning: during eviction there will be temporary increased backend reads for that key. proceed? :warning:

emily: proceed. issue eviction now.

sanjay: eviction complete. observed backend reads spike to fetch the blob but it finished and key removed from cache ring. memory pressure reduced on cache nodes.

jamie: metrics: total cache evictions +112%, node mem usage down 18%. overall 5xx reduced. good signal.

cora: drafting post for customers: short summary, root cause suspected: hot prefix causing cache thrash; actions taken: quarantine, eviction, rate-limits, fallback routing; ETA for full recovery 2 hours; point of contact support@redwood.com.

emily: temporary changes to revert at 2h if stable. plan to re-enable prefetch and remove quarantines gradually after observing 30m of stable p95 and 5xx < baseline.

alex: note for follow-up: need to implement automatic hot-prefix detection + quarantine + nicer customer-visible throttling. file a ticket to product to add this mitigation in autoscale toolkit.

incident-bot: oncall handoff: emily -> alex in 55 minutes. scheduled follow-up meeting in 30m.

jamie: FYI, I just saw one tenant attempt to exceed the new quota, got `429` and then circuit-breaking. no cascading failures.

cora: posted support updates and created postmortem doc skeleton: https://confluence.redwood/incidents/1801234567-hotkey-quarantine

emily: monitoring looks stable. continuing to observe. keeping channel open.

ops-bot: ACTION: create follow-up tasks: (1) postmortem owner=alex, (2) check cache eviction heuristics owner=sanjay, (3) product feature request owner=emily.

alex: assigning postmortem to myself. will coordinate with product and ops. thanks all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation in place, customer impact reduced, monitoring continuing. last update: 1801234890

emily: closing incident channel after 1h of stability. will publish postmortem in ~24h.

cora: closing support tickets with notes and follow-up communications queued.

jamie: nice work. learned a lot about prefix quarantine flow.

emily: closing the thread. good job team. :tada:
